retracted.reason: RETRACTED 2026-11-05. This ADMIT was not a comparison of anything: the control drifted -33.8% across the five repetitions (152.6, 152.0, 152.3, 126.1, 101.0 TFLOPS), so the baseline mean of 136.81 TFLOPS is a starved control, not a measurement of the machine at rest. Welch's t-test on two independent series attributes that drift to the candidate, which is exactly what 'independent' means, so no statistical gate could have caught it: the p-value of 0.0146 is an artifact of the starved control, not an effect of the power change. This run is the harness's OWN documented counter-example - harness/levers.py names it as 'a significant win bought with a starved control'. The honest figure for the same lever, measured on a stable control with both arms alternately in one session, is the paired re-measurement in optimize_20261104_102356.json.
